description: **June 18, 1815**, in one rainy day in Belgium, Napoleon's Empire collapsed. Waterloo closes the Hundred Days and opens a century of monarchical order in Europe.

hero.hook: One day of mud in Belgium, and the Empire collapses for good.

blocks.text: **June 18, 1815**, near the village of **Waterloo**, in Belgium, the destiny of Europe is being played out in the rain. **Napoleon** faces two enemies at once: the British **Arthur Wellesley**, Duke of **Wellington**, and the Prussian **Gebhard von Blücher**.
It's not just a defeat. It is the end of the First Empire. In one day, the man who had dominated Europe was shattered by mud, mistakes and an alliance that finally held together.

After his abdication of **April 1814**, Napoleon was exiled to the island of **Elbe**, off the coast of Italy. The winners redesign Europe at . **March 1, 1815**, he landed near Antibes. It's the beginning of the **Hundred Days**: the troops sent to stop him rally. He retakes Paris without bloodshed. [[The Congress of Vienna (1814-1815)]]

blocks.caption: The return of the island of Elba: Napoleon regains power.

blocks.text: Napoleon and Wellington had never met before Waterloo. The Belgian battlefield was their only face-to-face encounter.
Europe declared him “outlaw”. His plan: use the . The idea is simple. Place yourself between Wellington and Blücher, beat them one after the other, before they come together. [[Central position]]

sections.title: The return from the island of Elba

blocks.text: On **June 16**, Napoleon defeated the Prussians at **Ligny**, a Belgian village. The same day, , one of his bravest generals, held the British at **Quatre-Bras**, a strategic crossroads. But Napoleon believes the Prussians are out of action. He detaches Marshal **Grouchy** with **33,000 men** to pursue them. [[Marshal Ney]]
Some historians attribute the delay on the morning of June 18 to an attack of hemorrhoids which would have prevented Napoleon from riding on horseback for his usual reconnaissance.

The **18**, after a night of rain, he waits **11:30 a.m.** for the ground to dry. He wants to move his , a massive concentration of cannons. This delay gives Blücher time to walk towards the sound of the cannon. [[Large Battery]]

sections.title: Two days before: Ligny and Quatre-Bras

blocks.text: The battle begins around fortified farms: **Hougoumont** and the **Holy Hedge**. Ney's charges broke on the British , infantry formations in a rectangle, bayonets outwards. Around **4:30 p.m.**, the Prussians appear on the French right flank. Grouchy stays too far away. [[Square]]

As a last resort, Napoleon launched the **Imperial Guard**, his elite unit. For the first time, she steps back. The cry “The Guard retreats!” » triggers panic. Retirement becomes rout. Wellington and Blücher join at the **Belle-Alliance**.

sections.title: The day that broke the Empire

blocks.text: Napoleon abdicated on **June 22, 1815**. Exiled to **Saint Helena**, an isolated island in the South Atlantic, he died in **1821**. The Congress of Vienna imposes the [[Legitimacy]]: putting the royal dynasties back on their thrones. Russia, Austria and Prussia border the continent. This “European Concert” maintains relative peace until **1914**.

events.title: Waterloo

blocks.text: **Waterloo** (**June 18, 1815**) finishes off Napoleon. The delay of the attack, the absence of Grouchy and the junction of Wellington with Blücher caused the fall of the Empire and ushered in a century of monarchical order.
